_note: Hand-maintained list of former burial grounds / sites some buyers ask about. Coordinates and radii are APPROXIMATE centres of the historical site, from public sources — verify before relying on them. Add entries freely; radius_m is the rough extent of the former site.

sites.name: Bidadari Cemetery (former)
sites.note: Christian, Muslim, Hindu and Sinhalese sections; site is now Bidadari estate (Woodleigh / Upper Aljunied / Bidadari Park Dr).
sites.source_note: NLB Infopedia 'Bidadari Cemetery': at the base of Mount Vernon, bounded by Bartley Rd and Upper Serangoon Rd; Christian, Muslim, Hindu and Sinhalese sections; opened 1908, last burial 1972; exhumed 2001-2006 for housing. (Replaces a dead NLB link, checked 2026-10-09.)

sites.name: Mount Vernon Columbarium & crematorium (former)
sites.note: Closed 2018; land folded into the Bidadari development.
sites.source_note: NLB Infopedia 'Aljunied': Mount Vernon Crematorium at Upper Aljunied Rd opened 1962, closure announced 2003, cleared site for new housing. NEA (https://www.nea.gov.sg/our-services/after-death/mount-vernon-columbarium-relocation-programme): columbarium relocation programme ended December 2018. (Replaces Wikipedia, checked 2026-10-09.)

sites.name: Kwong Wai Siew Peck San Theng Cemetery (former) — Bishan
sites.note: Cantonese/Hakka cemetery over most of today's Bishan New Town (Bishan St 11–24, Sin Ming). The Peck San Theng temple/columbarium remains at Bishan St 22. Extent approximate: roughly Bishan St 11–25 south of Ang Mo Kio Ave 1.
sites.source_note: NLB Infopedia 'Bishan': Kwong Wai Siew Peck San Theng founded 1870 on the site of Bishan New Town for Cantonese and Hakka immigrants; no new burials from 1973; land acquired 1979; graves exhumed 1982-1984; clan kept 3.2 ha for a temple and columbarium. Street-level extent is our own estimate. (Replaces Wikipedia, checked 2026-10-09.)

sites.name: Tiong Bahru burial grounds (former)
sites.note: 'Tiong Bahru' = 'new cemetery' (Hokkien/Malay); the estate and Bukit Merah fringe were built over cleared burial land.
sites.source_note: NLB Infopedia 'Tiong Bahru': name from 'tiong' (cemetery) + 'bahru' (new); graves exhumed to Bukit Brown before the SIT estate was built (infrastructure by 1931, first block 1936). (Replaces a dead NLB link, checked 2026-10-09.)

sites.name: Bukit Brown / Kopi Sua Cemetery (mostly intact)
sites.period: 1922–1973 (still standing; partly cleared for Lornie Highway)
sites.note: Large Chinese cemetery west of Thomson; no HDB directly inside but blocks along Thomson/Sime Rd sit near its edge.
sites.source_note: NLB Infopedia 'Bukit Brown Municipal Cemetery': opened 1 January 1922, closed 1973; hill known as Kopi Sua; LTA's 2011 dual four-lane road (MacRitchie Viaduct to Adam Flyover) cut through part of it. (Replaces Wikipedia, checked 2026-10-09.)

sites.name: Jalan Kubor Cemetery (intact)
sites.note: Historic Malay/Muslim cemetery in Kampong Glam, next to Victoria St / Kallang Rd flats.
sites.source_note: NLB Infopedia 'Jalan Kubor Cemetery': oldest Muslim cemetery in Singapore, off Victoria Street near Kampong Glam; royal plot shown on an 1836 map; no longer in use, earmarked for housing since 1998. (Replaces Wikipedia, checked 2026-10-09.)

sites.name: Old Kallang / Geylang Bahru Chinese cemeteries (former)
sites.note: Several small clan burial grounds stood between Kallang Bahru and Geylang Bahru before the HDB estates; extent approximate.
sites.source_note: UNVERIFIED: this NLB link no longer resolves (404, checked 2026-10-09) and no official page was found that confirms these burial grounds. Re-source or remove.
